text:
lucy: FYI rolling out graceful-shutdown v1 on proxy-edge this morning caused weird session accounting on /v1/stream. Seeing dozens of "fresh" sessions per user during drain.
pranav: Is that the change that replies 204 + FIN for idle WS? I thought that was opt-in for long-poll only.
emma: It was enabled for a subset of routes in the canary group to reduce socket pile-up. Canary metrics show socket count down but sessions_started up 8x for affected tenants.
dan: Console shows tenants hitting quota because our billing pipeline counts session creation instead of resume. Are resume tokens being preserved on the close path?
lucy: digging: proxy responds 204 but we drop X-Resume-Token when synthesizing the close response. Client reconnect happens without token -> server makes brand new session.
pranav: Ugh. Two problems: proxy behavior and pipeline semantics. Short-term mitigation = revert graceful-shutdown for streaming routes in canary. Longer-term = two options: (A) preserve resume header + add heuristic header x-resume-hold-ms so clients can wait, (B) server-side tombstone map that treats reconnects within window as resumes even without token.
emma: Option A requires client libs to read x-resume-hold-ms, which we can't force immediately. Option B touches gateway hot path. How expensive would tombstones be?
dan: rough calc: store tombstone for N seconds per session id on close. At peak 100k sessions, 10s TTL -> ~100k entries, each small (48-64 bytes plus index) -> okay for gateway mem, but we'd need benchmark. Also requires adding metric tombstone_hits / tombstone_misses.
lucy: product ops wants route-level annotation showing "resume-aware" vs "fresh" sessions, and a dashboard line for duplicate_session_rate and billing_delta. They want to differentiate churn vs organic growth.
pranav: Also need a signal for "client resumed without token" so we can see how many clients would have benefited from x-resume-hold-ms. If that's tiny, prefer header approach + client lib release.
emma: I patched a quick telemetry flag to emit resume_hint when we see close-without-resume and immediate reconnect within 5s. Early canary shows resume_hint=true for ~12% of reconnects.
dan: 12% is nontrivial. We should rollback the graceful-shutdown on streaming routes while we decide. I'll open infra rollback.
ops-bot: Canary rollback triggered by dan at 1887654330 for proxy-edge-canary-3.
lucy: Rolling back now. Also adding alert: alert_duplicate_session_rate > 3% sustained 5m for streaming routes.
pranav: For the design doc: propose hybrid: keep proxy change but preserve resume token and emit x-resume-hold-ms=2000; gateway also implements tombstones but with a smaller default ttl (5s) behind a flag. That way clients that update get best UX, and gateway cover legacy clients.
emma: I'll wire the telemetry: new metrics resume_hints, tombstone_lookups, duplicate_session_rate, and a dashboard panel per-route.
dan: I'll simulate tombstone memory footprint with a small load test against gateway-local. If all green we can enable feature-flag for tombstones next week.
lucy: Action items: 1) rollback graceful-shutdown on streaming canary (done) 2) add alert panel (dan) 3) telemetry instrumentation (emma) 4) design PR for hybrid approach (pranav) 5) client note for honoring x-resume-hold-ms (lucy -> devex).
deploy-bot: Rollback completed: proxy-edge-canary-3 reverted at 1887654345.
lucy: thanks. tagging @oncall in case quota alerts flare. We'll reconvene after telemetry uplifts. :thumbsup:
